sec: HUS Triad, TTP Pentad & Types · p753

items.q: Every corner of the TTP pentagon is listed below EXCEPT:
items.exp: The pentagon carries thrombocytopenia, fever, MAHA, neurological symptoms (brain) and GI symptoms; renal failure is the third corner of the HUS triangle, not of the pentad. (Book p753)

items.q: What is written in square brackets beneath 'Neurological symptoms' in the TTP pentagon?
items.exp: The pentagon's vertex is labelled 'Neurological Symptoms [Brain]', localising the fifth feature of the TTP pentad. (Book p753)

items.q: In the TYPES table, what proportion of atypical HUS cases progress to ESRD?
items.exp: The prognosis row for atypical HUS/D− prints 'Bad (50% progress to ESRD)' along with increased chances of recurrence after renal transplant, while typical HUS is simply 'Good'. (Book p753)

items.q: A 34-year-old with dysentery-negative HUS is counselled before a living-related transplant. Which line of the TYPES table applies to him?
opts: Atypical HUS — any age, bad prognosis with increased recurrence after renal transplant
Typical HUS — childhood onset with good prognosis
Typical HUS — prognosis good because the cause is infection
Neither, since the table says nothing about transplantation
items.exp: The atypical column lists any-age onset, genetic (m/c) or sporadic drug-induced cause, bad prognosis with 50% progress to ESRD and increased chances of recurrence after renal transplant. (Book p753)
